record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Secured commitments from more than 250 hospitals to make hospital food healthier.
record.q: Secretary Kennedy Secures Commitments from More Than 250 Hospitals to Make Hospital Food Healthier

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Announced $96 million over four years for eight communities under the new STREETS program for people living on the streets with addiction or mental illness.
record.q: STREETS will provide $96 million over four years

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Proposed a rule requiring food makers to notify the FDA when they conclude an added ingredient is "Generally Recognized as Safe" (GRAS).
record.q: HHS proposed a rule requiring manufacturers to notify the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) when concluding that the use of a substance added to human or animal food is Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS)

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Deferred, with CMS, more than $1 billion in federal Medicaid payments to California and Minnesota until the states document certain high-risk claims.
record.q: today deferred more than $1 billion in federal Medicaid payments to California and Minnesota as the states submit additional documentation supporting certain high-risk Medicaid claims

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Signed determinations ending the COVID-19 Emergency Use Authorization declarations for drugs, biological products and medical devices.
record.q: Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has signed determinations terminating the COVID-19 Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) declarations for drugs and biological products and for medical devices

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Restored the Presidential Fitness Test and launched a "Get Kids Active" effort.
record.q: Secretary Kennedy Restores the Presidential Fitness Test, Launches Get Kids Active

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Testified before the Senate Finance Committee on the President's Fiscal Year 2027 HHS budget.

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Released the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025–2030 with Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, telling Americans to "eat real food."
record.q: Secretary Brooke Rollins today released the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025–2030, marking the most significant reset of federal nutrition policy in decades. The new Guidelines deliver a clear, common-sense message to the American people: eat real food.

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Announced with President Trump new actions on autism, including a first FDA-recognized treatment pathway and new research funding.
record.q: President Donald J. Trump and U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. announced bold new actions to confront the nation’s autism spectrum disorder (ASD) epidemic

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Began winding down mRNA vaccine development under BARDA, canceling and scaling back several contracts.
record.q: today announced the beginning of a coordinated wind-down of its mRNA vaccine development activities under the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA), including the cancellation and de-scoping of various contracts and solicitations

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Removed all 17 sitting members of the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), to be replaced with new members.
record.q: the agency removed the 17 sitting members of the ACIP committee and will replace them with new members

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: The MAHA Commission released its assessment of childhood chronic disease, naming poor diet, environmental toxins, too little physical activity, chronic stress and overmedicalization as contributing factors.
record.q: the report exposes a range of contributing factors—including poor diet, accumulation of environmental toxins, insufficient physical activity, chronic stress, and overmedicalization

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Testified before the Senate HELP Committee on the Fiscal Year 2026 HHS budget.
record.q: Department of Health and Human Services Budget Date: Wednesday, May 14th, 2025

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: HHS announced the FDA would begin removing concentrated ingestible fluoride prescription drug products for children from the market.
record.q: today announced that it is initiating action to remove concentrated ingestible fluoride prescription drug products for children from the market

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Announced, with the FDA, new measures to phase out all petroleum-based synthetic dyes from the nation's food supply.
record.q: today announced a series of new measures to phase out all petroleum-based synthetic dyes from the nation’s food supply

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Announced a restructuring of HHS that cut about 10,000 full-time jobs and merged its 28 divisions into 15, including a new Administration for a Healthy America; HHS said the change would save taxpayers $1.8 billion a year.
record.q: it will save taxpayers $1.8 billion per year through a reduction in workforce of about 10,000 full-time employees

record.office: Secretary of Health and Human Services
record.t: Was confirmed by the Senate as Secretary of Health and Human Services by a vote of 52 to 48.
record.q: The United States Senate today confirmed Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to serve as Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) by a vote of 52-48.
